jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. The campus has produced five Nobel laureates and is known for its academic achievement, premier research, innovation and anteater mascot. Led by Chancellor Howard Gillman, UC Irvine has more than 36,000 students and offers 224 degree programs. It’s located in one of the world’s safest and most economically vibrant communities and is Orange County’s second-largest employer, contributing $7 billion annually to the local economy and $8 billion statewide.

To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

The School of Physical Sciences (SoPS) aims to deliver scientific breakthroughs that reshape our understanding of the physical world and provide solutions to the most profound problems of our age. We achieve this by asking hard questions; setting inspiring, visionary goals; and cultivating an inclusive, interdisciplinary culture that is open to broad ideas. We advance humanity through a deeper understanding of the physical science that governs the world. Our flagship projects not only directly address some of today's most fundamental and existential problems, but also strive for their impactful applied solutions.

The SoPS develops philanthropic priorities that will empower the school to elevate its strong academics and research to elite levels of excellence. From predicting cancer tumor growth with mathematics to exploring the possibility of life on other planets and finding solutions to the effects of climate change, our researchers in the top-ranked departments of Chemistry, Earth System Science, Mathematics, and Physics & Astronomy are blazing new pathways every day. Our world-renowned faculty bridge fields through interdisciplinary collaborations with engineers, computer scientists, biologists, social scientists and many others. This out-of-the-box thinking and our standing commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion propels our research and enables cutting-edge science to advance our mission.

Within the SoPS, the Office of Advancement is our comprehensive fundraising operation. This includes alumni relations and development, in strong partnership with the Director of Communications for the SoPS. With support from the University of California, Irvine Office of University Advancement, our staff partner with donors, alumni, faculty, and school senior leadership to secure philanthropic resources for the school of physical sciences and its departments.

Your Role on the Team

The School of Physical Sciences (SoPS) is seeking a development professional who works collaboratively with the Executive Director of Development (EDoD), the Director of Communications for the SoPS, and University Advancement (UA) to contribute to the development program and secure significant philanthropic investments to support the SoPS. The primary activity of the Director of Development (DoD) is externally focused to secure private philanthropic support and the DoD's effectiveness will be evaluated on the ability to achieve financial goals and meet metrics. Under the general direction of the EDoD, the DoD develops strategies to manage and enhance the annual fund and major gifts programs for the SoPS. The DoD is expected to serve as a member of the School's Advancement team, and to also be a highly collaborative colleague with other development officers across the campus. Our office works on coordinated hybrid schedules to meet the business needs of leadership and our clients. This position will begin on-site and - with leadership approval - may be eligible for a hybrid schedule of no less than three days on site per week.

Essential Functions

The identification of essential functions below is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties that may be assigned to this position, nor does it restrict the duties which may be assigned to this position if such duties reasonably relate to the position.

Plans, organizes, and directs large-scale, fundraising campaigns which include multiple components, including related special event planning. May serve as an expert or lead development professional in a specific academic discipline. Develops and coordinates guest and participant lists, including developing and maintaining databases of participants, potential and invited speakers, faculty, and administrators. Tracks responses to invitations, sends reminders, guidance and other information to participants, guests, and leadership. Staffs and serves as event lead for logistics during event functions. Attend and arrange additional event staffing. Recruit, train, and support new and repeat student, faculty and staff volunteers needed for each event. Coordinates and arranges travel, lodging meals as needed. 25%

Ensures that predetermined fundraising goals are met and implements program activities to achieve these goals. Conducts at least 12 substantive meaningful contacts per month; Qualifies 40 new major gift prospects through personal appointments, annually; Secures $1,000,000 annually in new gifts and commitments for the SoPS 30%

Develops and manages a dynamic major gift portfolio to identify, qualify, cultivate, directly solicit and steward prospects with the capacity to make contributions of at least $25,000. May include corporate and foundation prospects, and contributions at a variety of levels. Writes proposals for solicitation of individual, corporate, and/or foundation prospects. 20%

Works with the Executive Director of Development, the Dean, department chairs, and center directors to identify, assess, and prioritize funding opportunities within the School. Fosters successful fundraising in the School by preparing the Dean and other academic leaders to participate routinely and effectively in development activities and prospect appointments. Works routinely and closely with academic leadership, key faculty, and Advancement colleagues to support the Dean's fundraising priorities including administrative and operational needs of the department. In collaboration with the Director of Communications, prepares PowerPoint presentations, speaking engagement materials (including speaking remarks and faculty bios) for the Dean, manages resources, develops, and implements procedures for internal records management for donor events. 10%

Collaborates with various UA offices and functions - including stewardship, research and prospect management, financial services, annual giving, and development to advance prospect strategies; Uses the UA prospect management and tracking system. Participates as directed by the Executive Director of Development, as a member of the UA constituent development team in development activities across campus and serves as a resource to other unit-based development colleagues about the School’s fundraising opportunities. Manages prospect and donor contacts, contact reports, and donor proposals. Assists in identifying relevant alumni from the SoPS four departments and prospective donors, including basic prospect research. Manages multi-step gift processing (including deposits), ensuring compliance with School of Physical Sciences and University policies and procedures. Works with School fund manager to ensure timely gift reporting for school leadership. Assists in the development and distribution of appropriate stewardship and fund-raising materials including gift stewardship letters. Works in, updates and produces reports in Zotforce (Salesforce). Manage and prepare data/reports for fundraising initiatives as directed. Attends functions, meetings, and serves on internal/external committees as a representative of the School. 10%

Manages, builds, and leads the SoPS development boards. 5%

Required

What It Takes to be Successful

Advanced knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations concepts, principles, and procedures. Ability to apply creative techniques to the processes.
Advanced written, oral and interpersonal communication skills, including political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships throughout the organization and with outside constituencies. Ability to make persuasive and compelling presentations of goals and objectives in order to secure gifts.
Persuasive executive communication skills
Advanced organizational, analytical, and critical thinking skills, including skill in creative and effective decision-making and problem identification/avoidance/resolution, and strong project management skills.
Very strong skills in maintaining confidentiality.
Ability to prepare complex and detailed proposals and related materials.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively with both school and institution to achieve goals, and to meet metrics and deadlines. Ability to meet demanding work schedule expectations.
Highly organized, focused, and goal-oriented with the ability to prioritize and handle multiple projects.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Salesforce or a comparable donor/prospect database system.
Demonstrable experience in stewardship plans leading to additional investments.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
A minimum of 5 years of experienceof successful professional development and/or fundraising-related experience, OR, any equivalent combinations of education and/or experience from which comparable knowledge, skill and abilities have been achieved. Related experience and comparable knowledge should include fundraising, and may also include fundraising in combination with a variety of pathways including - but not limited to - executive events planning and management, administrative coordination, annual giving, stewardship, external relations, communication, public relations, corporate/foundation relations, development personnel, and others.

Preferred

Advanced working knowledge of all aspects of the location, including current issues of concern for both the campus throughout higher education generally.
Advanced working knowledge of the location, its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure. Interest and/or familiarity in the sciences and the local Orange County philanthropic and business community.
Advanced knowledge of applicable laws, rules, regulations, policies, etc.
A minimum of 5 years of experiencesuccessful professional development and/or fundraising-related experience in higher education

Special Conditions

Local, regional, and/or national travel is required.
May work long hours to meet fundraising commitments.

These benefits may include medical insurance, sick and vacation time, retirement savings plans, and access to a number of discounts and perks. Please utilize the links listed here to learn more about our compensation practices and benefits.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Global Sourcing & COE
jobs.description:
Accelerate your career. Join the organization that's driving the world's technology and shape the future.

Ingram Micro is a leading technology company for the global information technology ecosystem. With the ability to reach nearly 90% of the global population, we play a vital role in the worldwide IT sales channel, bringing products and services from technology manufacturers and cloud providers to business-to-business technology experts. Our market reach, diverse solutions and services portfolio, and digital platform Ingram Micro Xvantage™ set us apart. Learn more at www.ingrammicro.com.

Come join our team where you’ll make technology happen in surprising ways. Let’s shape tomorrow - it’ll be a fun journey!

This role reports to the VP of Strategic Sourcing and is responsible for leading Global Strategic Sourcing for the Professional Services and Marketing categories, leading the India Sourcing organization, and continue to develop a Global Sourcing Center of Excellence that drives improved capabilities, scalability, and value creation across the Global Sourcing team and key cross-functional stakeholders. The Executive Director will establish the global vision, operating model, and transformation roadmap, partnering with senior leadership and key cross functional teams. (Global Platform Group, Finance, Legal, Ops, HR, etc.) to deliver enterprise-wide impact across cost, risk, innovation, and supplier value. Within the first year, the Executive Director is expected to establish the operating foundation, demonstrate early savings wins, and deliver a clear roadmap to drive value creation.

Your role:

Lead global sourcing for the Professional Services and Marketing categories including over $150M in global annual spend.

Develop and execute global category strategies across Professional Services and Marketing, segmenting suppliers by value tier and aligning sourcing plans to business priorities and market dynamics.
Lead sourcing initiatives and negotiate best-in-class agreements leveraging should-cost models, RFPs, and advanced analytics to drive total cost of ownership reduction and deliver year-over-year savings targets.
Manage supplier performance through defined SLAs, KPI scorecards, and structured business reviews, driving continuous improvement and accountability across the supply base.
Build and maintain strategic supplier relationships that deliver value across cost, quality, service levels, risk, and innovation, partnering with internal stakeholders to align supplier capabilities with business needs.
Monitor and mitigate supply risk, leveraging market intelligence, inflation mitigation strategies, and escalation/de-escalation mechanisms to ensure supply continuity and competitive pricing.

Lead and manage the India Sourcing team:

Provide direct leadership, coaching, and development for the India-based sourcing team, setting clear objectives, performance expectations, and career development plans to build a high-performing organization.
Define and align the India sourcing team’s scope, workload, and priorities with the global sourcing strategy, ensuring effective coverage across assigned categories, regions, and operational functions.
Partner with India-based leadership and HR to navigate local labor practices, compliance requirements, and organizational norms, while integrating the team into the broader global sourcing operating model.
Drive capability building within the India team through training, process standardization, and adoption of global tools, systems, and best practices to elevate sourcing competency and execution quality.
Establish and track team KPIs, including sourcing cycle times, savings delivery, contract coverage, and stakeholder satisfaction, reporting performance to senior leadership on a regular cadence.

Lead the development of a Global Sourcing Center of Excellence:

Create a Global Center of Excellence to enable the Global Sourcing team to achieve key best-in-class results through developing and implementing best practice standards in Global Sourcing processes, systems/tools, data, analytics, and reporting.
Develop and implement best practice processes across the Global Sourcing team for key processes such as strategic sourcing, category strategy development, supplier performance management, supplier contract development, cost savings tracking, project tracking and updates, business case development, etc. Work to standardize the processes across all Global Sourcing categories and with stakeholders globally. Leverage AI, robotics, and other techniques to automate key processes where possible.
Develop plans to fully leverage existing systems and tools that provide the Global Sourcing team key global data/information, analytical systems/tools, and advance analytics capabilities to track performance, track compliance to supplier agreements, support initiatives, and proactively assess issues and opportunities. Evaluate, secure approval, and implement new and/or improved systems and tools to provide needed information and system capabilities.
Create an analysis and reporting center of excellence including a central repository for key data/info, KPI reporting, performance dashboards, savings tracking, supplier scorecards, etc.
Develop and implement a Global Sourcing Playbook that informs and enables non-Sourcing stakeholders globally to conduct key sourcing activities (eg. RFPs) for small and/or low complexity initiatives.

What you bring to the role:

Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, or Procurement or equivalent. MBA a plus.
15+ years of experience with increasing leadership responsibilities, and a minimum of 5 years in a supervisory/management level position.
Strong Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Relationship Management skills.
Excellent business acumen, financial, cost modeling, data analysis, and root cause problem solving skills.
Experience negotiating complex contracts including strategic partnerships, pricing, SLAs, and other terms and conditions.
Ability to track and manage supplier performance and set expectations for improvement.
Demonstrated ability to effectively identify, evaluate and implement solutions for customers.
Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of end-to-end processes, determining business requirements, and process improvement.
Supports and promotes cross functional team efforts, acting as process architect and organizational change agent.
Experience leading cross-functional teams to deploy, sustain, and improve on investments from tools, people, and processes.
Works with executives and operational stakeholders to ensure cross-functional understanding and cooperation to execute highly complex deployment and transformation initiatives in a global matrixed environment.
Highly self-motivated, consultative approach, enthusiastic and ability to create followership, and lives the “continuous improvement” philosophy and can drive change successfully, push back with alternate approaches or solutions, and constantly challenges others to strive for improvement.
Help define transformational strategies, ensure resource alignment, and successfully manages the transition, adaptation, and adoption of processes and functionality.
Proactive, well organized, logical and creative thinker, with demonstrated ability to function effectively in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities, and with strong result orientation - has track record for delivering results, takes ownership & is accountable.
Strong presentation and written communication skills, influencing skills, and the ability to work successfully with all levels of the organization.
Excellent training and facilitation, time and project management skills.
Proven track record of integrity, sound judgment, organization building success.
Excellent personal leadership skills – proven ability to build, develop and motivate a team.

Position requires occasional travel, up to 25% of the time.

Our purpose – Opening up a world of opportunity – explains why we exist. Here at HSBC we use our unique expertise, capabilities, breadth and perspectives to open up new kinds of opportunity for our more than 40 million customers. We’re bringing together the people, ideas and capital that nurture progress and growth, helping to create a better world – for our customers, our people, our investors, our communities and the planet we all share.

Managing Director, Technology Media & Telecommunications (“TMT”) Banking will be responsible for leading and managing the coverage of relationships across the TMT sector within Corporate & Institutional Banking (“CIB”). Maintain HSBC internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators
Undertake all required activities as directed by line manager or as agreed in annual objectives in support of the furthering of the TMT and CIB business

Ability to develop a strategic dialogue with clients
Industry expert

jobs.description:
About Brooklyn Boatworks
Brooklyn Boatworks (BKBW) harnesses the unique craft of wooden boatbuilding and maritime-centered exploration to inspire young people to uncover the confidence, skills, and courage to chart pathways to success in and outside the classroom. Through hands-on boatbuilding, sailing, and career exploration, BKBW engages hundreds of New York City students annually in meaningful, project-based learning.

Position Summary
Brooklyn Boatworks seeks an experienced, mission-driven Development Director to serve as a key member of the organization’s leadership team. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Development Director will lead fundraising strategy, systems, and execution while building the relationships and internal infrastructure needed to support Brooklyn Boatworks’ next phase of growth.

This is a meaningful opportunity for a hands-on development professional to strengthen and professionalize fundraising operations for one of New York City’s most distinctive youth development organizations. The Development Director will supervise the Development Coordinator and partner closely with the Executive Director, Resource Development Committee, and Board to expand contributed revenue, deepen donor engagement, and ensure Brooklyn Boatworks has the resources needed to advance its mission.

The Development Director will oversee annual fundraising planning, donor cultivation and stewardship, grants and institutional funding, campaigns and events, CRM and data tracking, acknowledgments, and development communications to meet a $1.5M revenue goal in FY 2026-2027. The role will also prepare Board-facing materials and help translate fundraising strategy into clear opportunities for Board engagement.

This position requires some evening and weekend work.
To apply for this position please send a cover letter and resume to inquiries@brooklynboatworks.org. Please do not apply via the linkedin portal.

We will begin reviewing applications as they are received. Early applications are strongly encouraged.

Key Responsibilities
Fundraising Strategy & Planning
Develop and manage an annual development plan with clear revenue goals, timelines, strategies, and accountability measures.
Partner with the Executive Director,Resource Development Committee, and Development Coordinator to align fundraising priorities with organizational strategy.
Track progress against goals and use data to guide decisions, identify gaps, and adjust strategies.

Individual Giving, Donor Relations & Stewardship
Manage donor cultivation, solicitation, acknowledgment, and stewardship across individual giving programs.
Build and maintain a healthy donor pipeline, including prospects, current donors, lapsed donors, and major gift opportunities.
Prepare donor communications, meeting briefings, follow-up materials, and stewardship touchpoints.

Grants, Institutional Funding & Development Communications
Support research, writing, submission, and reporting for foundation, corporate, government, and other institutional funding opportunities.
Collaborate with program and communications staff to gather stories, statistics, outcomes, and impact data for proposals, reports, appeals, and marketing materials.
Ensure development communications are accurate, compelling, timely, and aligned with Brooklyn Boatworks’ mission and voice.

Events, Campaigns & Community Engagement
Lead the development and execution of fundraising events, campaigns, and appeals, including writing compelling donor communications, solicitation materials, and campaign messaging.
Work with Board members and volunteers to identify prospects, make introductions, host or attend cultivation opportunities, and support donor stewardship.
Represent Brooklyn Boatworks with donors, funders, partners, and community stakeholders.

Systems, Operations & Board Support
Maintain and improve development systems, including CRM/data entry standards, donor records, gift tracking, reporting, and follow-up workflows.
Ensure timely and accurate acknowledgments, stewardship records, pledge tracking, and documentation of donor and prospect activity.
Prepare Board and Resource Development Committee materials, including pipeline updates, progress reports, prospect lists, meeting briefings, and action items.
Help translate fundraising strategy into clear, manageable Board participation opportunities, including introductions, cultivation, stewardship, and event support.
Support strong internal coordination by working closely with the Executive Director, program staff, finance, communications, and Board leadership.
Supervise, support, and help prioritize the work of a Development Coordinator, including gift processing, data entry, acknowledgments, event support, and administrative follow-up.

The responsibilities above are intended to provide an overview of the role and are not an exhaustive list of duties.
Qualifications
Commitment to youth development, hands-on learning, and Brooklyn Boatworks’ mission
7–10 years of fundraising experience with proven success driving $3M+ revenue
Demonstrated success in securing major gifts, corporate partnerships, and/or foundation/government grants
Excellent storyteller and relationship builder; confident engaging donors and Board members
Strategic thinker with strong operational skills, project management, and CRM proficiency

Benefits
Brooklyn Boatworks offers a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with employer match, and paid time off.
Salary Range: $110,000 - $115,000.

Apply today to join an amazing team, dedicated to advocating the health & well-being of individuals, families, and communities. The Mental Health Association of Columbia-Greene Counties Inc. is looking to fill a full-time Residential Program Director position.

MHACG's Licensed Treatment Community Residence provides rehabilitative support, recovery, and clinical services for those with severe, persistent mental illness. Staff are on duty 24 hours with on-call procedures for emergency situations. The Program is to enhance the options of participants for choosing, accessing, and maintaining preferred permanent housing, and to provide the support needed to maximize the recipient's successful integration into independent community living. WISE Seeks an Executive Director

About the Organization

For more than 50 years, WISE has been a steadfast advocate for survivors of domestic and sexual violence, stalking, and trafficking, while serving as a regional leader in prevention education, legal advocacy, restorative practices, and community engagement. Across 23 communities in New Hampshire and Vermont’s Upper Valley, WISE works to build safer, more just communities where all people can live free from violence and abuse.
Since its founding in 1971, WISE has supported more than 10,000 survivors, trained over 5,000 first responders and other professionals, taught healthy relationship skills to more than 18,000 students, and engaged more than 11,000 community members through workshops, education, and outreach.
At the heart of WISE is a belief that how the work is done is as important as the work itself. The organization strives to model the values and relationships it seeks to cultivate, recognizing that authentic connection, mutual respect, and shared accountability are essential to lasting change. Guided by the values of Courage, Compassion, Connection, and Curiosity, WISE fosters a culture that is deeply collaborative, mission-driven, and rooted in the transformative power of community.
WISE enters this leadership transition from a position of considerable strength, with healthy finances, an engaged board, talented and committed staff, deep community trust, and a reputation for innovation and excellence. WISE is overseen by a dynamic, highly attentive 13-member board of directors. WISE employs 22 staff, many longstanding and widely recognized as experts in their area of work. Staff are described as professional, extremely supportive, friendly, deeply caring, and closely connected to the mission.

WISE operates with an annual budget of approximately $2.2 million and stable finances, including properties that provide emergency housing. WISE’s work is sustained through a diverse and robust funding portfolio that includes foundation and government grants, and individual contributions. For more information about WISE, visit the WISE website.

The Opportunity

WISE seeks an exceptional leader to guide WISE into its next chapter of impact and innovation, recognizing we live in a world of increasing complexity and uncertainty. Following a long-tenured and highly respected leader whose influence has shaped the organization's culture, reputation, and relationships, the next Executive Director will inherit an organization deeply rooted in its survivor-centered approach and commitment to addressing the root causes of domestic violence and relationship abuse. Organizational Overview: Bernie’s Book Bank

Better futures begin with books.

Bernie's Book Bank
is a mission-driven organization dedicated to ensuring that every child has access to books and the opportunity to build a home library of their own. Founded in Lake Bluff, Illinois in 2009, Bernie's Book Bank has delivered more than 32 million free, high-quality books to children through a growing network of schools, early childhood programs, hospitals, clinics, and community partners. Each child receives eight free books a year, matched to their reading level, hand-delivered, every year from birth through sixth grade, to keep.

The organization is focused on a simple but consequential idea: children who have books of their own are better positioned to develop the literacy skills they need to succeed. Bernie's Book Bank prioritizes children and communities with the greatest need, including Title I schools and low-income communities where children may otherwise have limited access to books.

Recent independent research
has further validated the impact of this approach. In April 2026, a five-year randomized controlled trial of the program was published in PNAS stating that children who received books every year gained roughly half to two thirds of an additional year of reading growth, reinforcing the organization's belief that book ownership is a meaningful and scalable intervention.

Today, Bernie's Book Bank operates through a national chapter model, with Chicago serving as its flagship and most mature market. The organization also has chapters in Milwaukee and the Florida Suncoast, with an ambitious vision for continued national growth. The Chicagoland Chapter serves roughly 315,000 children a year across a six-county service area, and will hand-deliver approximately 2.5 million books to them in 2026. Across all three chapters, the plan for 2026 is to deliver roughly 3 million books to approximately 375,000 children, putting millions of books directly into the hands of those who need them most.

Bernie's Book Bank is entering an important new chapter. With a strong operating model, a compelling body of evidence, deep community relationships, and an ambitious goal of reaching one million children nationally by 2029, the organization is building the infrastructure and leadership capacity needed to grow its impact. This includes strengthening its national systems while ensuring that the Chicago chapter remains a strong, well-supported, and appropriately resourced foundation for that growth.

Position Summary: Executive Director, Chicagoland Chapter

The Executive Director, Chicagoland Chapter, joins Bernie's Book Bank at an important moment in the organization's evolution. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Director will serve as the senior leader of the organization's flagship chapter and will have primary responsibility for its financial sustainability, fundraising, operations, external relationships, and continued growth.

This is an opportunity for a leader who is energized by growth, comfortable with change, and excited by the opportunity to take a well-performing chapter to its next level of success and mission impact. Above all, the Executive Director will help ensure that Chicago remains a powerful engine for Bernie's Book Bank while serving as a strong advocate for the chapter as the organization continues to build its national footprint.

Partner with the CEO and national leadership on enterprise growth, contributing to the development of a national infrastructure while helping ensure that the lessons, relationships, and practices developed in Chicago inform the organization's broader growth.
Provide strong operational leadership, partnering with the Senior Operations Manager and broader operations team to ensure that fundraising and program growth translate into efficient and effective book processing, volunteer engagement, distribution, and community impact.

The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and 182 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org

VPU Context:
The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) is a shared commitment to end the world’s learning crisis. It is the only global partnership and fund dedicated entirely to helping children in lower-income countries get a quality education, so they can unlock their potential and contribute to building a better world.

We bring together governments, teachers, civil society, donors, United Nations agencies, development banks, businesses and private foundations to transform education systems so that every girl and boy can have hope, opportunity and agency.

What We Do

GPE helps low- and lower-middle-income countries build stronger education systems so that all children can get the education they need to thrive. We support more than 90 countries where the needs are greatest and focus on reaching the children who are the most vulnerable, including girls, children with disabilities, and those affected by extreme poverty or conflict. Our unique approach works. Between 2021 and 2025, GPE supported 372 million children in partner countries to get a better education through grants and co-financing.

How We Work

GPE is working to help governments transform their education systems to get the most vulnerable children in school, improve teaching and learning, and build equitable, inclusive and resilient education systems fit for the 21st century. Transforming education is about creating lasting changes and achieving impact on a scale. GPE sets out to deliver this transformative change by convening partners, mobilizing funds and catalyzing reforms to help partner countries accelerate access, learning outcomes and gender equality.

Multiply Possibility – Financing GPE 2030

GPE launched its 5th financing campaign for 2026-2030, co-hosted by Italy and Nigeria, to mobilize $5 billion for inclusive, high-performing education systems in the world’s most challenging contexts. This funding will unlock $15 billion in total education investment through co-financing and multiplier effects. A fully funded GPE will transform education systems and multiply possibility for 750 million children in 96 countries.

Governance And Organizational Arrangements

The GPE Board of Directors includes ministerial-level board members and alternates representing 20 constituencies that reflect the partnership’s breadth. The Board Chair is H.E. President Jakaya Kikwete and the Board Vice Chair is Ms. Christine Hogan. The Board of Directors, with its standing committees, provides policy and strategic oversight and approves or delegates funding decisions.

The GPE Secretariat, with 160 employees and hosted by the World Bank, is responsible for translating the policies and strategies set by the Board into practical support for partner countries, coordinating with diverse stakeholders and galvanizing global support for SDG 4. The Secretariat’s headquarters are in the World Bank’s offices in Washington, D.C., with a European office in Paris, an African office in Nairobi, a satellite office in Brussels, and a support office in Chennai.

Description

ABOUT THE JOB

The School of Physical Sciences (SoPS) aims to deliver scientific breakthroughs that reshape our understanding of the physical world and provide solutions to the most profound problems of our age. We achieve this by asking hard questions; setting inspiring, visionary goals; and cultivating an inclusive, interdisciplinary culture that is open to broad ideas. We advance humanity through a deeper understanding of the physical science that governs the world. Our flagship projects not only directly address some of today's most fundamental and existential problems, but also strive for their impactful applied solutions.

The SoPS develops philanthropic priorities that will empower the school to elevate its strong academics and research to elite levels of excellence. Our world-renowned faculty bridge fields through interdisciplinary collaborations with engineers, computer scientists, biologists, social scientists and many others. This out-of-the-box thinking and our standing commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion propels our research and enables cutting-edge science to advance our mission.

Within the SoPS, the Office of Advancement is our comprehensive fundraising operation. Lead global sourcing for the Professional Services and Marketing categories including over $150M in global annual spend.

Develop and execute global category strategies across Professional Services and Marketing, segmenting suppliers by value tier and aligning sourcing plans to business priorities and market dynamics.
Lead sourcing initiatives and negotiate best-in-class agreements leveraging should-cost models, RFPs, and advanced analytics to drive total cost of ownership reduction and deliver year-over-year savings targets.
Manage supplier performance through defined SLAs, KPI scorecards, and structured business reviews, driving continuous improvement and accountability across the supply base.
Build and maintain strategic supplier relationships that deliver value across cost, quality, service levels, risk, and innovation, partnering with internal stakeholders to align supplier capabilities with business needs.
Monitor and mitigate supply risk, leveraging market intelligence, inflation mitigation strategies, and escalation/de-escalation mechanisms to ensure supply continuity and competitive pricing.

Provide direct leadership, coaching, and development for the India-based sourcing team, setting clear objectives, performance expectations, and career development plans to build a high-performing organization.

Drive capability building within the India team through training, process standardization, and adoption of global tools, systems, and best practices to elevate sourcing competency and execution quality.
Establish and track team KPIs, including sourcing cycle times, savings delivery, contract coverage, and stakeholder satisfaction, reporting performance to senior leadership on a regular cadence.

About Brooklyn Boatworks
Brooklyn Boatworks (BKBW) harnesses the unique craft of wooden boatbuilding and maritime-centered exploration to inspire young people to uncover the confidence, skills, and courage to chart pathways to success in and outside the classroom. Through hands-on boatbuilding, sailing, and career exploration, BKBW engages hundreds of New York City students annually in meaningful, project-based learning.

Position Summary
Brooklyn Boatworks seeks an experienced, mission-driven Development Director to serve as a key member of the organization’s leadership team. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Development Director will lead fundraising strategy, systems, and execution while building the relationships and internal infrastructure needed to support Brooklyn Boatworks’ next phase of growth.

This is a meaningful opportunity for a hands-on development professional to strengthen and professionalize fundraising operations for one of New York City’s most distinctive youth development organizations. The Development Director will supervise the Development Coordinator and partner closely with the Executive Director, Resource Development Committee, and Board to expand contributed revenue, deepen donor engagement, and ensure Brooklyn Boatworks has the resources needed to advance its mission.

The Development Director will oversee annual fundraising planning, donor cultivation and stewardship, grants and institutional funding, campaigns and events, CRM and data tracking, acknowledgments, and development communications to meet a $1.5M revenue goal in FY 2026-2027. The role will also prepare Board-facing materials and help translate fundraising strategy into clear opportunities for Board engagement.

This position requires some evening and weekend work.
To apply for this position please send a cover letter and resume to inquiries@brooklynboatworks.org. Please do not apply via the linkedin portal.

We will begin reviewing applications as they are received. Early applications are strongly encouraged.

Key Responsibilities
Fundraising Strategy & Planning
Develop and manage an annual development plan with clear revenue goals, timelines, strategies, and accountability measures.
Partner with the Executive Director,Resource Development Committee, and Development Coordinator to align fundraising priorities with organizational strategy.
Track progress against goals and use data to guide decisions, identify gaps, and adjust strategies.

Individual Giving, Donor Relations & Stewardship
Manage donor cultivation, solicitation, acknowledgment, and stewardship across individual giving programs.
Build and maintain a healthy donor pipeline, including prospects, current donors, lapsed donors, and major gift opportunities.
Prepare donor communications, meeting briefings, follow-up materials, and stewardship touchpoints.

Grants, Institutional Funding & Development Communications
Support research, writing, submission, and reporting for foundation, corporate, government, and other institutional funding opportunities.
Collaborate with program and communications staff to gather stories, statistics, outcomes, and impact data for proposals, reports, appeals, and marketing materials.
Ensure development communications are accurate, compelling, timely, and aligned with Brooklyn Boatworks’ mission and voice.

Events, Campaigns & Community Engagement
Lead the development and execution of fundraising events, campaigns, and appeals, including writing compelling donor communications, solicitation materials, and campaign messaging.
Work with Board members and volunteers to identify prospects, make introductions, host or attend cultivation opportunities, and support donor stewardship.
Represent Brooklyn Boatworks with donors, funders, partners, and community stakeholders.

Systems, Operations & Board Support
Maintain and improve development systems, including CRM/data entry standards, donor records, gift tracking, reporting, and follow-up workflows.
Ensure timely and accurate acknowledgments, stewardship records, pledge tracking, and documentation of donor and prospect activity.
Prepare Board and Resource Development Committee materials, including pipeline updates, progress reports, prospect lists, meeting briefings, and action items.
Help translate fundraising strategy into clear, manageable Board participation opportunities, including introductions, cultivation, stewardship, and event support.
Support strong internal coordination by working closely with the Executive Director, program staff, finance, communications, and Board leadership.
Supervise, support, and help prioritize the work of a Development Coordinator, including gift processing, data entry, acknowledgments, event support, and administrative follow-up.

Commitment to youth development, hands-on learning, and Brooklyn Boatworks’ mission
7–10 years of fundraising experience with proven success driving $3M+ revenue
Demonstrated success in securing major gifts, corporate partnerships, and/or foundation/government grants
Excellent storyteller and relationship builder; confident engaging donors and Board members
Strategic thinker with strong operational skills, project management, and CRM proficiency

Impact the Future of Affordable Housing Across Pennsylvania

The Housing Alliance of Pennsylvania is seeking an accomplished, collaborative, and strategic Executive 
Director to lead a statewide organization dedicated to ensuring that all Pennsylvanians, especially those living on low incomes, have access to safe, decent, accessible, and affordable homes.

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as the organization’s leader, 
spokesperson, and public face, providing strategic direction while working closely with staff, members, 
policymakers, funders, and partners throughout Pennsylvania.
This is an opportunity for an experienced leader to build upon the Housing Alliance’s strong foundation and statewide presence while advancing housing policy, strengthening advocacy, engaging members and partners, developing resources, and bringing together diverse voices around the shared goal of making a home within reach of every Pennsylvanian.

If you are energized by bringing people together, influencing public policy, building meaningful partnerships, and creating statewide impact through housing advocacy and community development, we invite you to explore this leadership opportunity.

Why the Housing Alliance of Pennsylvania?

The Housing Alliance provides a unique opportunity to lead a respected statewide coalition working at the 
intersection of housing, public policy, advocacy, education, and community development. The organization brings together members and partners from Pennsylvania’s urban, suburban, and rural communities to advance policies, practices, and resources that address affordable housing, homelessness, homeownership, blight, and related community development issues.

The next Executive Director will have the opportunity to build upon this established statewide network while strengthening the organization’s voice, expanding its impact, and ensuring the Housing Alliance remains a trusted resource and effective advocate for housing throughout Pennsylvania.

Your Leadership Opportunity

The Housing Alliance is seeking a visible, engaged, and strategic leader who can bring together public policy expertise, coalition building, advocacy, organizational leadership, financial stewardship, and strong communication.

Success will ultimately be measured by the organization’s ability to bring diverse interests together, influence housing policy and resources, strengthen its statewide coalition, and advance meaningful solutions that help ensure every Pennsylvanian has access to a safe and affordable home.

WISE Seeks an Executive Director

About the Organization

For more than 50 years, WISE has been a steadfast advocate for survivors of domestic and sexual violence, stalking, and trafficking, while serving as a regional leader in prevention education, legal advocacy, restorative practices, and community engagement. Across 23 communities in New Hampshire and Vermont’s Upper Valley, WISE works to build safer, more just communities where all people can live free from violence and abuse.
Since its founding in 1971, WISE has supported more than 10,000 survivors, trained over 5,000 first responders and other professionals, taught healthy relationship skills to more than 18,000 students, and engaged more than 11,000 community members through workshops, education, and outreach.
At the heart of WISE is a belief that how the work is done is as important as the work itself. The organization strives to model the values and relationships it seeks to cultivate, recognizing that authentic connection, mutual respect, and shared accountability are essential to lasting change. Guided by the values of Courage, Compassion, Connection, and Curiosity, WISE fosters a culture that is deeply collaborative, mission-driven, and rooted in the transformative power of community.
WISE enters this leadership transition from a position of considerable strength, with healthy finances, an engaged board, talented and committed staff, deep community trust, and a reputation for innovation and excellence. WISE is overseen by a dynamic, highly attentive 13-member board of directors. WISE employs 22 staff, many longstanding and widely recognized as experts in their area of work. Staff are described as professional, extremely supportive, friendly, deeply caring, and closely connected to the mission.

WISE operates with an annual budget of approximately $2.2 million and stable finances, including properties that provide emergency housing. WISE’s work is sustained through a diverse and robust funding portfolio that includes foundation and government grants, and individual contributions. For more information about WISE, visit the WISE website.

The Opportunity

WISE seeks an exceptional leader to guide WISE into its next chapter of impact and innovation, recognizing we live in a world of increasing complexity and uncertainty. Following a long-tenured and highly respected leader whose influence has shaped the organization's culture, reputation, and relationships, the next Executive Director will inherit an organization deeply rooted in its survivor-centered approach and commitment to addressing the root causes of domestic violence and relationship abuse. The new Executive Director will have the opportunity to:
Preserve WISE’s valued culture while guiding the organization through forward-looking change and growth. WISE’s next leader will partner with the Board and staff to plan and shape the future of survivor services, balancing innovation and growth with organizational stability, mission alignment, and the values and approaches that have made WISE successful.
Lead a financially strong and operationally sound organization, while managing uncertainty surrounding public funding, grant requirements, compliance obligations, and changing regulatory environments.
Steward, strengthen and grow critical relationships with funders, coalition partners, community leaders, donors, and stakeholders.
Advance innovative programs and emerging areas of practice, including prevention education, restorative approaches, legal advocacy, and community education.
Expand community partnerships, collaborations and adult educational outreach, and explore opportunities to deepen public engagement and visibility.
Navigate increasing political polarization, and evolving public discourse over issues related to domestic and sexual violence and prevention education.
Build upon WISE's reputation and role as a regional and statewide leader in survivor advocacy, prevention education, and systems change.
Ensure WISE remains accessible, connected, and responsive to an increasingly diverse community, continuing its commitment to fairness, inclusiveness, and survivor-centered practice.
Support and develop a talented, mission-driven staff within the values and culture that have made WISE successful.
Leverage an engaged, talented, and supportive board, dedicated volunteers, and strong philanthropic relationships to advance strategic priorities.

The Ideal Candidate

WISE seeks a leader who combines strategic vision with humility, compassion, and a deep commitment to relationship-centered leadership. Candidates must bring the curiosity, perspective, and leadership necessary to help WISE to continue to evolve and thrive. The strongest candidates will demonstrate:

Mission and Values Alignment

Genuine commitment to supporting survivors and ending domestic and sexual violence.
Understanding of trauma-informed, survivor-centered practices.
Ability to lead with courage, compassion, connection and curiosity.
Commitment to fairness, inclusiveness, and dignity.

Highly Relational, Collaborative Leadership

Exceptional relationship-building skills and the ability to cultivate trust and partnerships across diverse stakeholders: staff, board members, donors, volunteers, survivors, public policy representatives, nonprofit and coalition partners, and community leaders.
Proven success leading, supporting, and growing teams.
A facilitative leadership style that empowers others and thrives in a collaborative thinking and decision-making environment.

Compelling Public-Facing Presence and Communication Skills

Proven success as a visible, approachable, and collaborative ambassador, with strong communication capabilities for public speaking, storytelling, and sharing the needs of survivors.
Experience sustaining and building external partnerships and leveraging the talents of others.

Strategic and Comfortable with Complexity

Ability to think and act strategically and leverage opportunities for partnerships and resources.
Proven experience bringing fresh perspective and thoughtful innovation to an organization.
Experience navigating complex political and funding realities, ambiguity, and competing priorities.
Curiosity and a thirst for learning about community needs, new approaches, staff wellbeing, and effective management.
Courage to make difficult decisions while remaining collaborative and transparent.

Strong Nonprofit Acumen

Understanding of nonprofit funding models, grant management, and protocols for compliance.
Sufficient financial literacy to oversee a complex organization, including budgets, audits, fundraising, and long-term sustainability.
10 years of senior leadership and management experience.

Adaptable and Empathetic Leadership

Experience fostering an organizational culture that centers dignity, safety, and respect.
Sound judgment, calmness, steadiness, and resilience under pressure.
Leadership that is fair, caring, shows humility in personal and organizational relationships, and respects organizational history and institutional knowledge.
Commitment to listening first, understanding culture, and leading thoughtfully.
Honors shared humanity of “those served and those serving.”

Organizational Overview: Bernie’s Book Bank

Better futures begin with books.

Bernie's Book Bank
is a mission-driven organization dedicated to ensuring that every child has access to books and the opportunity to build a home library of their own. Founded in Lake Bluff, Illinois in 2009, Bernie's Book Bank has delivered more than 32 million free, high-quality books to children through a growing network of schools, early childhood programs, hospitals, clinics, and community partners. Each child receives eight free books a year, matched to their reading level, hand-delivered, every year from birth through sixth grade, to keep.

The organization is focused on a simple but consequential idea: children who have books of their own are better positioned to develop the literacy skills they need to succeed. Bernie's Book Bank prioritizes children and communities with the greatest need, including Title I schools and low-income communities where children may otherwise have limited access to books.

Recent independent research
has further validated the impact of this approach. In April 2026, a five-year randomized controlled trial of the program was published in PNAS stating that children who received books every year gained roughly half to two thirds of an additional year of reading growth, reinforcing the organization's belief that book ownership is a meaningful and scalable intervention.

Today, Bernie's Book Bank operates through a national chapter model, with Chicago serving as its flagship and most mature market. The organization also has chapters in Milwaukee and the Florida Suncoast, with an ambitious vision for continued national growth. The Chicagoland Chapter serves roughly 315,000 children a year across a six-county service area, and will hand-deliver approximately 2.5 million books to them in 2026. Across all three chapters, the plan for 2026 is to deliver roughly 3 million books to approximately 375,000 children, putting millions of books directly into the hands of those who need them most.

Bernie's Book Bank is entering an important new chapter. With a strong operating model, a compelling body of evidence, deep community relationships, and an ambitious goal of reaching one million children nationally by 2029, the organization is building the infrastructure and leadership capacity needed to grow its impact. This includes strengthening its national systems while ensuring that the Chicago chapter remains a strong, well-supported, and appropriately resourced foundation for that growth.

Position Summary: Executive Director, Chicagoland Chapter

The Executive Director, Chicagoland Chapter, joins Bernie's Book Bank at an important moment in the organization's evolution. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Executive Director will serve as the senior leader of the organization's flagship chapter and will have primary responsibility for its financial sustainability, fundraising, operations, external relationships, and continued growth.

This is a highly external-facing, development-forward leadership opportunity. The Executive Director will inherit a base of philanthropic, corporate, and community relationships, while also having the opportunity to build a more sophisticated and diversified development operation. The successful candidate will be a visible leader in the Chicagoland community, personally cultivating relationships with high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners.

Additionally, the Executive Director will serve internally as the chief operator, leading across functions and overseeing the Chicagoland Chapter's approximately $5 million budget. The Executive Director will manage organizational priorities, support a talented team, and ensure that revenue growth translates into programmatic growth.

This is an opportunity for a leader who is energized by growth, comfortable with change, and excited by the opportunity to take a well-performing chapter to its next level of success and mission impact. Above all, the Executive Director will help ensure that Chicago remains a powerful engine for Bernie's Book Bank while serving as a strong advocate for the chapter as the organization continues to build its national footprint.

Key responsibilities include:
Partner with the CEO and national leadership on enterprise growth, contributing to the development of a national infrastructure while helping ensure that the lessons, relationships, and practices developed in Chicago inform the organization's broader growth.
Provide strong operational leadership, partnering with the Senior Operations Manager and broader operations team to ensure that fundraising and program growth translate into efficient and effective book processing, volunteer engagement, distribution, and community impact.
Lead the Chicagoland Chapter's fundraising and revenue strategy, establishing annual and multi-year goals and personally driving major individual, corporate, foundation, and partnership opportunities.
Build and manage a significant portfolio of donors and prospects, cultivating high-capacity individuals, corporate leaders, foundations, and community partners and personally soliciting and stewarding major commitments.
Partner with the Founder on the transition of long-standing donor relationships into a managed Chicagoland portfolio, treated as a deliberate program with named relationships and timelines rather than a one-time handoff.
Diversify and strengthen the chapter's revenue model, developing new opportunities across major gifts, corporate partnerships, sponsorships, foundations, events, and volunteer-to-donor engagement.
Build a high-performing development function, assessing the current structure, identifying gaps, recruiting key talent, and establishing the systems, roles, goals, and accountability needed to support sustained growth.
Serve as the senior external leader for Chicago, representing Bernie's Book Bank with donors, corporate and civic leaders, philanthropic institutions, community organizations, media, and other key stakeholders across Chicagoland.
Lead and engage the Chicagoland Board, partnering with the Board to strengthen its transition from an advisory body to a governing board and activating members as ambassadors, donors, connectors, event participants, and fundraisers.
Lead chapter financial stewardship, overseeing budgeting, forecasting, revenue performance, and financial decision-making in partnership with national finance leadership.

Build a strong and connected team culture, providing clarity, accountability, and support while maintaining the collaborative, flexible, and mission-driven culture that characterizes the Chicago team.

Description

The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and 182 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org

VPU Context:
The Global Partnership for Education (GPE) is a shared commitment to end the world’s learning crisis. It is the only global partnership and fund dedicated entirely to helping children in lower-income countries get a quality education, so they can unlock their potential and contribute to building a better world.

We bring together governments, teachers, civil society, donors, United Nations agencies, development banks, businesses and private foundations to transform education systems so that every girl and boy can have hope, opportunity and agency.

What We Do

GPE helps low- and lower-middle-income countries build stronger education systems so that all children can get the education they need to thrive. We support more than 90 countries where the needs are greatest and focus on reaching the children who are the most vulnerable, including girls, children with disabilities, and those affected by extreme poverty or conflict. Our unique approach works. Between 2021 and 2025, GPE supported 372 million children in partner countries to get a better education through grants and co-financing.

How We Work

GPE is working to help governments transform their education systems to get the most vulnerable children in school, improve teaching and learning, and build equitable, inclusive and resilient education systems fit for the 21st century. Transforming education is about creating lasting changes and achieving impact on a scale. GPE sets out to deliver this transformative change by convening partners, mobilizing funds and catalyzing reforms to help partner countries accelerate access, learning outcomes and gender equality.

Multiply Possibility – Financing GPE 2030

GPE launched its 5th financing campaign for 2026-2030, co-hosted by Italy and Nigeria, to mobilize $5 billion for inclusive, high-performing education systems in the world’s most challenging contexts. This funding will unlock $15 billion in total education investment through co-financing and multiplier effects. A fully funded GPE will transform education systems and multiply possibility for 750 million children in 96 countries.

Governance And Organizational Arrangements

The GPE Board of Directors includes ministerial-level board members and alternates representing 20 constituencies that reflect the partnership’s breadth. The Board Chair is H.E. President Jakaya Kikwete and the Board Vice Chair is Ms. Christine Hogan. The Board of Directors, with its standing committees, provides policy and strategic oversight and approves or delegates funding decisions.

The GPE Secretariat, with 160 employees and hosted by the World Bank, is responsible for translating the policies and strategies set by the Board into practical support for partner countries, coordinating with diverse stakeholders and galvanizing global support for SDG 4. The Secretariat’s headquarters are in the World Bank’s offices in Washington, D.C., with a European office in Paris, an African office in Nairobi, a satellite office in Brussels, and a support office in Chennai.

Description

ABOUT THE JOB

The Deputy Chief Executive Officer (DCEO) reports to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and shares with the CEO responsibility for leading, managing and representing GPE. The role sits between strategy and execution, translating Board direction and CEO vision into a functioning, coordinated system across a complex partnership model. The DCEO is accountable for making the system work end-to-end, ensuring countries, grant agents, and partners operate coherently, and turning strategy into results.

The DCEO directly supervises all managers, including the COO, CFO and CTO, who oversee the full breadth of GPE operations. The DCEO also serves as the manager of the Executive Office and the Governance Team that supports the Board of Directors. The DCEO is an ex-officio member of the Board of Directors and the Board’s Executive Committee.

The DCEO represents GPE in various international fora, coordinates high level relationships, and manages a diverse body of work. He/she also oversees the GPE management team and is responsible for ensuring organizational coherence.

Duties And Accountabilities

Provide Strategic and policy direction:

With the CEO, helps shape and approve strategic direction and policy development.
Advises strategic, policy and operational matters before the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee.
Under GPE2030, ensures programs and organizational units are aligned with and maximizes the impact of the three strategic objectives on education reform, finance and partnership.
Champions gender equality and inclusion in all aspects of GPE’s work.

Represent GPE To External Audiences And Partners:

Represents GPE in international fora, including the Sherpa committee of the SDG4 High-level Steering Committee
Engages with senior government officials of donor and partner countries, and leadership in INGOs, foundations and private firms.
Provides leadership to GPE’s efforts to raise critical resources for the GPE Fund and for co-financing.

Lead Secretariat Operations:

Oversees the breadth of Secretariat functions and operations related to regional/country programs, governance, personnel and organizational development, finance and grants, external relations, evaluation, monitoring and data management.
Ensures internal alignment, cross-team coordination, clear workflows, and efficient processes.
Oversees and drives efforts to improve the coherence, efficiency and cost-effectiveness of Secretariat operations.

Manage Corporate Governance:

Manages the governance team
Manages governance operations related to the Board of Directors and its committees.
Supports and advises the Chair and Vice Chair in their Board duties.
Ensures the Secretariat provides strategic, high-quality and timely documentation to facilitate Board and committee deliberations.
Supports the Vice Chair in their role as Chair of the Executive Committee.

Oversees Portfolio Performance And Delivery:

Ensures the grant portfolio is on track, and corrective action is taken as needed.

Ensures quality and timeliness of partnership compacts, grant applications, and implementation progress. Intervenes when programs stall; grant agents underperform or country processes break down.

Orchestrates The GPE Operating Model:

Ensures clarity on roles, decision rights and escalation pathways.
Encourages partner alignment behind country priorities
Ensures coherence across funding windows
Strengthens the effectiveness of the model by reducing fragmentation, improving clarity and efficiency, and reducing competing incentives.

Oversee Results, Data, And Performance Management:

Holds partners accountable for delivery timelines, quality of implementation, results reporting.
Ensures strong monitoring frameworks, reliable data flows from countries and grant agents, and performance tracking across the portfolio.
Provides data and reporting to shape Board discussions and make strategic adjustments.

Manage Risks:

Identifies and mitigates political risk, operational risk, governance risk, financial risk, PSEAH and reputational risks to GPE.

Selection Criteria

The incumbent needs to be able to interact effectively with clients, teams and managers, and international partners to find practical solutions to problems, and to facilitate quick results, all in response to a complex and constantly evolving environment.

The Frick Pittsburgh Museums and Gardens is the steward of the collections and 10-acre estate of Helen Clay Frick in the East End of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. About Seaview

Seaview is an award-winning, New York City based production company that has grown into a dynamic entertainment enterprise spanning theater, film, and television. Founded 11 years ago, Seaview has built its reputation on bold storytelling and creative innovation. 

The Opportunity

Seaview is seeking an experienced, strategic, and financially sophisticated COO to serve as the key executor of and thought partner to the CEO's strategic vision. The ideal candidate pairs a sharp business mind with a genuine love of the creative process - someone who thrives in creative environments, loves working with artists and producers, and knows how to balance financial discipline with ambition and fun. This is a rare opportunity to help shape the next chapter of one of the most dynamic companies in live entertainment.

Key Responsibilities

Executive & Operational Leadership

Manage all day-to-day operations, ensuring cohesion between creative, strategic, and financial priorities.
Serve as the CEO's internal operating and strategic partner - collaborating to prioritize big ideas, work through problems and analyze industry trends, and translate Seaview's vision into actionable, measurable outcomes, including new opportunities and verticals that expand the company's reach and enterprise value.
In collaboration with the CEO, serve as the primary liaison between the company and its Board of Directors, including regularly reporting up to and interfacing with the Board on financial health, key initiatives, and general company updates.
Formalize and maintain organizational structure - overseeing roles, decision-making authority, and reporting lines - while serving as an accessible, trusted presence for all staff.
Own the company's internal meeting cadence and collaborative tools, ensuring company priorities and context are clearly and consistently communicated across departments; attend departmental meetings with the CEO and department heads as needed.
Ensure decisions and commitments translate into clear ownership, deadlines, and follow-through across the organization.
Manage external operational partners, including legal counsel, finance and business management support, and human resources vendors.
Build and sustain a vibrant, collaborative company culture grounded in creativity, curiosity, and high performance.

Strategic Financial Planning & Management

In collaboration with external business management support:

Own a current, complete view of Seaview's financial position across company decision-making and project realities, advising the CEO and department heads on key financial issues, including project-level decisions.
Develop and maintain the company's core budgeting documents:
Revenue Management: project-by-project revenue modeling across theatrical, film, TV, and general management, in coordination with department heads; maintain a rolling 12–24 month revenue outlook synthesizing actuals with forward projections
P&L Management: maintain and revise the annual operating budget monthly, tracking variance against prior projections and monitoring balance-sheet spend sent to production entities
Cash Flow: maintain a rolling 12+ month cash position projection and proactively communicate funding needs and timing to the CEO, department heads, and business management
Conduct a monthly review of the general ledger, P&L, and balance sheet; and proactively flag revenue or spending areas requiring CEO attention.
Own Seaview's production investments portfolio, including paperwork and tracking systems.
Manage Seaview's external financial partners, including the bookkeeping and accounting resources and the general management partners handling project-related accounting.

People Management Processes

In collaboration with external HR support and advisors:

Lead organizational design and higher-order people strategy, including management coaching, talent development, team structure, succession planning, and culture, in coordination with the CEO.
Own the employee lifecycle end-to-end, including recruitment, hiring, and onboarding of employees and contractors, annual reviews and ongoing development check-ins, performance and staffing issues, and day-to-day HR administration including PTO requests, Paid Family Leave planning, and employee complaint handling.
Establish and maintain the policies governing personnel costs and operating expenses, including compensation structure, headcount planning, bonus criteria, and expense approval thresholds and oversee monthly tracking against them.
Administration and execution of employee reviews and ongoing development check-ins, and managing high-level staffing concerns and performance issues as they arise.

Legal & Business Affairs Oversight

In collaboration with external legal counsel:

Oversee all corporate legal matters for the company and its productions, including reviewing and negotiating agreements between Seaview and production partners, vendor agreements and partnerships, investments into productions, and corporate transactions.
Work closely with internal stakeholders and external counsel to manage risk and protect the company’s interests across all divisions and in harmony with the Board of Directors.

Production Support

Maintain a broad, non-creative overview of all Seaview productions, across verticals, providing advice and oversight where needed.
At critical moments, step in as a hands-on problem solver, helping teams navigate challenges quickly and effectively.

Qualifications

10+ years of senior leadership experience in entertainment, media, or related industries (theater experience highly preferred).
Proven track record leading finance, operations, and legal/business affairs across a multi-division organization.
Experience building and scaling systems, processes, and teams in high-growth environments.
Strong communication and relationship-management skills, with the judgment to manage both up and across an organization.
MBA or JD is of interest, but not required.

Ideal Candidate

You are a big-picture thinker who is equally at home in the details — forward-looking and open-minded, but pragmatic and grounded in how you actually get things done. You bring real operational rigor and financial sophistication to the role, balanced by a calm, organized, and consistent hand day to day. You lead people the way you'd want to be led: direct and candid, but supportive, empathetic, and genuinely comfortable empowering others rather than holding on tightly. You build trust through transparency — your team always knows where they stand with you. You move quickly and adapt readily, but you're judicious about it, weighing decisions rather than reacting to them. You're as comfortable in a boardroom as you are at an opening night party, and you bring the same warmth, curiosity, and reliability to both.

Participation in Seaview’s medical, dental, and vision plans.
